ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, and UBOs against (i) FINTRAC customer due diligence guidance, (ii) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and its regulations, (iii) the Criminal Code terrorist entities list, (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, (v) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and (vi) recognized domestic and international PEP databases. Pre-incorporation screening is documented and archived, with ongoing transaction monitoring once payment rails (Stripe, AdSense) are activated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – 'Registre des entreprises' online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative: Corporations Canada / NUANS portal via Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (www.ic.gc.ca).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c. S-31.1), the corporate legal name must be in French and must include a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée', 'Limitée', 'Compagnie', or 'Corporation'. Non-French distinctive elements are permitted only where the name is deemed bilingual or includes an established transliteration; all filings and public documents must be in French or accompanied by a certified French translation. Federally incorporated corporations may adopt English or French legal names, but names are rejected if confusing with existing trademarks, business names, or registered entities; a NUANS name search report is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal by the Registraire des entreprises, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire within 30 days of receipt of the refusal notice, setting out arguments and alternative names; the Registraire must issue a reasoned decision. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec within 60 days of the denial. For federal name refusals, the applicant may file an objection with the Director of Corporations Canada within 30 days and thereafter seek judicial review in the Federal Court under the Canada Business Corporations Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk digital publishing industry, provided the registered office is a real physical street address in Quebec where service of process can be accepted; reputable virtual office and registered agent services offering mail forwarding and attended reception in Quebec are accepted by the REQ and financial institutions if mail forwarding arrangements are contractually documented. A post office box is not acceptable as a registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – estimated annual likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection is below 10% (approximately 5%) for a low-risk ISIC 5813 digital publishing entity with no cash-intensive operations; Revenu Québec and FINTRAC generally increase scrutiny only upon anomalous transaction patterns, unpaid tax filings, or registry inconsistencies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec for Quebec provincial QST and corporate income tax administration. Portals: CRA 'My Business Account' at canada.ca and Revenu Québec 'Clic Revenu' at revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada must first obtain a Canadian federal Business Number (BN) through CRA, generally by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or through the CRA online registration service. Where taxable Canadian supplies exceed the small supplier threshold (CAD 30,000), the entity must register for GST/HST under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. For Quebec, the entity must separately register for QST with Revenu Québec using the same BN prefix and a QST account, typically through the Registraire d'entreprises or Form LM-1/VF. The corporation should also file a federal corporate income tax account (T2) and, if carrying on business in Quebec, a Quebec provincial corporate tax account (CO-17). A non-resident corporation must also complete Form RC258 or applicable waiver filings to establish its Canadian reporting obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a check-the-box regime comparable to the United States. A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is automatically a taxpayer resident in Canada and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Available statutory elections include: (i) the Section 216 Income Tax Act election for a non-resident to file a Canadian return on net rental income; (ii) the Section 219 election for a non-resident corporation regarding taxable Canadian earnings; (iii) the GST/HST 'closely related corporation' election under Section 156 Excise Tax Act, permitting certain intercompany supplies to be deemed for nil consideration; and (iv) the QST-related elections under Quebec's Taxation Act and QST legislation harmonized with the Excise Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch elections are available; Canada and Quebec apply specific anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (Canadian dollars) in worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters for GST/HST; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies to taxable supplies made in Quebec for QST registration, with QST applying on Quebec supplies at 9.975% on the selling price excluding GST. Digital magazine subscriptions and sponsored media placement revenues are generally taxable supplies subject to registration once the threshold is exceeded, subject to specific place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API validation for GST/QST invoices. However, registrants must retain electronic records and invoices in a readable format, and GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE when gross revenue exceeds CAD 1.5 million. Revenu Québec requires mandatory electronic filing of QST returns for large businesses and for those required to remit through the EFT system. Standard business-to-business invoicing must contain the registrant's BN/GST/HST registration number and, where applicable, the QST registration number, but no real-time clearance or approval is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered Canadian/Quebec supplier may zero-rate the supply of digital magazine subscriptions and online sponsored media placement services when the supply is made to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST/QST and who is not present in Canada at the time the supply is made, and when the intangible property or service is not used in Canada. For digital publications and e-media, the supplier must establish that the recipient's ordinary place of abode or business is outside Canada and that the supply is not related to Canadian real property or tangible personal property located in Canada at the time of supply. The zero-rating applies to intangible personal property and services supplied to non-residents under Schedule VI, Part V and Part X, Excise Tax Act, and to corresponding QST provisions in the Quebec Taxation Act. Proof of non-resident status must be retained in the taxpayer's books, including IP address verification, billing address, subscriber registration data, contract terms, and payment settlement records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial invoice with explicit reference to zero-rated supply
Non-resident subscriber or advertiser registration and address records
Digital delivery logs and IP address verification for online transmissions
Contract or terms of service evidencing supply to a non-resident recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rated export claim if documentary evidence is incomplete, contradictory, or unavailable. Misclassification of domestic taxable supply as zero-rated export attracts reassessment of unpaid GST/HST/QST, interest, and penalties. Gross negligence penalties under Section 285 Excise Tax Act and Section 1051 Quebec Taxation Act may be up to 200% of the tax sought, and criminal tax evasion penalties include fines up to CAD 1 million or 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Historical clawback for unrepatriated foreign currency proceeds, failure to meet the 180-day inward remittance requirement, or failure to substantiate the non-resident status of the recipient may result in full reversal of the zero-rating, loss of input tax credits, and additional penalties for false statements or omissions under Sections 327 and 328 Excise Tax Act and corresponding Quebec provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Canada is Canada's central bank and oversees monetary policy and key payment-system functions. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated banks. The Autorité des marchés financiers regulates financial services within Quebec, including relevant provincial financial-market activities. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for current- and capital-account transactions; Canada has no general capital controls or requirement for prior central-bank approval of ordinary cross-border investment, borrowing, dividends, or loan repayments. Banks must apply sanctions, anti-money-laundering, beneficial-ownership, and transaction-monitoring rules. A Canadian corporation may remit dividends or other lawful payments abroad subject to corporate-law solvency requirements, board authorization, contractual restrictions, and applicable Canadian withholding tax. Treaty relief may reduce withholding on qualifying payments when beneficial-ownership and residence documentation is provided. Interest, royalties, service fees, and related-party payments require appropriate legal, transfer-pricing, and tax support; tax filings and withholding obligations may apply. Quebec incorporation does not create a distinct currency-control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory deadline requiring exporters to repatriate export proceeds and no mandatory foreign-currency conversion or surrender ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the account holder's discretion, subject to contractual, sanctions, tax, and financial-reporting obligations. Canadian financial institutions may request invoices, contracts, shipping evidence, and payment-purpose information for compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection or payouts and Low as a substitute for a Canadian corporate bank account. Canadian payment service providers must comply with applicable federal retail-payment supervision requirements where in scope, and money-services businesses may require FINTRAC registration. An offshore electronic-money institution is not automatically authorized to provide regulated services in Canada or to hold deposits. Confirm the provider's Canadian permissions, safeguarding arrangements, client-fund protections, CAD settlement capability, and correspondent-bank access. Stripe and Google AdSense payouts are subject to provider eligibility, account-name matching, tax documentation, and supported payout methods; neither replaces the corporation's own banking and tax-compliance obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory requirement that every director appear physically to open a Canadian corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available at a bank's discretion, but the bank can require an in-person meeting, Canadian address evidence, certified identity documents, or additional verification, particularly for non-resident directors, foreign ownership, or complex control structures. Requirements vary by institution and account product; confirm directly with the selected bank before incorporation or travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, layered foreign entities, or inability to identify individuals with significant control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide articles and certificate of incorporation, current corporate profile, securities register or equivalent ownership records, register of individuals with significant control where applicable, ownership chart through all intermediate entities, constitutional documents for owners, and identity and address evidence for directors, signing officers, and beneficial owners. Disclose control rights and explain any nominee or trust arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or owners, remote-only application, or mismatched corporate and residential addresses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide valid government-issued identification, independent proof of residential address, Canadian registered-office and operating-address evidence, board resolutions, corporate contact details, and a concise explanation of the business's Canadian nexus and why remote onboarding is requested. Supply certified translations where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained initial capital, large or rapid incoming wires, or funds originating from unrelated third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide investor subscription or shareholder-loan agreements, board approvals, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, originating account statements, wire instructions, and an ownership-to-sender reconciliation. Use accounts held in the corporation's legal name and pre-notify the receiving bank of material transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital publishing or sponsored-media receipts inconsistent with stated activity, including platform payouts, advertising proceeds, or high-volume international payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the business plan, website and publication details, publisher and advertiser contracts, platform statements, invoices, campaign records, customer and geographic profiles, expected payment volumes, and a documented explanation of payment flows. Retain records supporting the commercial purpose and counterparty identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure, high-risk counterparties, adverse media, or payments involving restricted jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide counterparty identity and ownership information, contracts and invoices, screening results, end-use and geographic details, and documented escalation and approval records. Do not process a transaction prohibited by Canadian sanctions or other applicable law; obtain specialist advice where restrictions or ownership rules are uncertain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a bank account in the Canadian corporation's exact legal name and receive funds by SWIFT or another bank-supported cross-border wire. Identify the transfer accurately as share subscription proceeds, paid-in capital, or shareholder-loan proceeds; Canada has no universal statutory FX purpose-code system for these transactions. Provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, board authorization, investor identity and ownership details, source-of-funds evidence, originating-bank details, and expected amount and timing. Do not characterize debt as equity or vice versa. Reconcile receipts to the corporation's accounting records and maintain evidence for tax, corporate-law, and bank review. Check intermediary-bank fees, currency conversion spreads, and cut-off times before initiation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary supplier, contractor, advertising, and platform payments, use bank wire/SWIFT, eligible domestic electronic transfers, or a regulated payment provider, matching the beneficiary's name and account details to the contract and invoice. SWIFT MT103 is a customer credit-transfer message format, not an independent settlement system or guarantee of payment. For material trade or service obligations, a commercial letter of credit may be arranged through a bank subject to credit approval, documentary terms, and applicable ICC rules where incorporated. Retain contracts, invoices, proof of service or delivery, tax documentation, and approval records. For dividends, interest, royalties, and related-party fees, confirm corporate authorization, solvency, withholding-tax treatment, treaty eligibility, and required tax filings before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a bank or appropriately regulated provider, generally supported by identifiable foreign-currency exposures and counterparty documentation
Non-deliverable forwards where offered and lawful for the relevant currency and counterparty; settlement is cash-based and may be subject to additional counterparty and product restrictions
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management or currency funding, subject to bank approval and documented treasury purpose
Currency options where offered by an eligible counterparty, subject to product suitability, contractual documentation, collateral, and applicable derivatives-reporting or conduct requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (LPLE) and the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA, CQLR c S-31.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the enterprise's registration date (LPLE s. 36; QBCA s. 89)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of C$16 per month, capped at C$160; two consecutive years of non-filing permit the REQ to dissolve the enterprise (LPLE s. 58), terminating legal personality, banking facilities, and contract standing; directors remain exposed to offence-level fines and liability for corporate obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - applicable where the entity is incorporated federally with extra-provincial registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada - Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation (CBCA s. 263.3; Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: C$25 late-filing fee; failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution; revival requires C$200 plus C$5 per month of dissolution, all outstanding annual returns, and Director approval; officers/directors are subject to summary-conviction fines up to C$5,000 (CBCA s. 123).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return - T2 (federal) and CO-17 (Quebec), including financial statements and Small Business Deduction reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) jointly with Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (ITA s. 150; Taxation Act, CQLR c I-3, s. 1000); tax balance due within 3 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the Small Business Deduction, otherwise within 2 months (ITA s. 157)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (max 12 months); repeat-offender penalty of 10% plus 2% per month (ITA s. 162); parallel Quebec penalty regime; failure to file after formal demand triggers arbitrary assessment by CRA/Revenu Québec and director liability for unremitted instalments and source deductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No asset or revenue threshold applies at the private-company level. A statutory audit is mandatory when: (i) the corporation is a reporting issuer or distributes securities to the public; (ii) shareholders holding at least 10% of votes (QBCA) or 5% (CBCA) validly demand an audit; or (iii) shareholders do not unanimously waive the auditor appointment at the annual meeting. Private corporations maintain the standard practice of an annual unanimous shareholder waiver; unaudited financial statements still require director approval and presentation to shareholders (QBCA s. 219; CBCA s. 155).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I); private enterprises may elect ASPE (Part II) or IFRS. Records must support the T2/CO-17 returns, Small Business Deduction computation, CCA pool balances, and GST/HST filings. ITA s. 230 prescribes a 6-year statutory retention minimum; the pipeline applies a 7-year enterprise retention standard.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 6 months after fiscal year-end for both federal and provincial filings

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of tax payable per month, up to 12 months; plus interest on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 to Canada Revenue Agency with supporting documentation and Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) to claim reduced rates under applicable DTAs
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory, reduced to 0% or 5% under treaties; Interest: 25% statutory, reduced to 0% or 10% under treaties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income or overstatement of deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction with fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for penalties, restitution, and potential criminal charges

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length transfer prices without documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments to income, penalties up to 10% of transaction value, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Potential personal liability for negligence or willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not filing corporate tax return by deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 5% per month of unpaid tax, up to 12 months, plus interest
